rules.mechanism: OPEC+ members account for a large share of world crude output, so quota changes alter global supply.

conditions.note: Actual supply change depends on compliance with announced quotas and spare capacity.

rules.rationale: Producer-group supply decisions are a primary driver of crude balances.

rules.mechanism: With relatively inelastic short-run demand, lower supply tends to raise the clearing price and higher supply to lower it.

conditions.note: Inventories, demand shocks and expectations can dominate.

rules.rationale: Basic supply-demand mechanics of a commodity market with inelastic short-run demand.

rules.mechanism: Traders price the risk of future supply disruption into crude futures.

conditions.note: Premium often fades if physical supply is not actually disrupted.

rules.mechanism: Jet fuel / ATF is refined from crude, so its price tracks crude plus a refining crack spread.

conditions.note: Crack spreads and (in India) ATF taxation modify pass-through.

rules.rationale: Refined product prices are anchored to crude input costs.

rules.mechanism: Fuel is typically one of the largest airline operating-cost items.

conditions.note: Fuel hedging delays and dampens the effect.

rules.mechanism: Higher costs compress margins unless airlines pass them on through fares or fuel surcharges.

conditions.note: Pass-through depends on demand strength and competition.

rules.rationale: Margin = revenue - costs; incomplete pass-through squeezes margins.

rules.mechanism: India imports most of the crude it consumes, so a higher price raises the import bill for given volumes.

conditions.note: Applies globally because India is a price-taker; strongest relevance when the event involves India.

rules.rationale: Import bill = price x volume; India is a large net crude importer.

rules.mechanism: A larger oil import bill widens the trade deficit and hence the current account deficit.

conditions.note: Services exports and remittances can offset.

rules.mechanism: A wider current account deficit increases dollar demand from importers, pressuring the rupee.

conditions.note: RBI FX intervention and capital inflows can offset.

rules.rationale: External financing needs affect currency demand.

rules.mechanism: Fuel and transport costs feed into consumer prices directly and via second-round effects.

conditions.note: Retail fuel prices in India are partly administered, which delays pass-through.

rules.rationale: Energy weight in CPI and input-cost pass-through.

rules.mechanism: Gasoline is a component of US CPI, so crude prices pass through to headline inflation.

conditions.note: Core inflation is much less sensitive than headline.

rules.mechanism: Producers sell crude at prices linked to benchmarks, so realisations rise with the oil price.

conditions.note: Windfall taxes, hedging and production volumes modify the effect.

rules.mechanism: When retail fuel prices are held steady, higher crude costs squeeze state-run OMC marketing margins.

conditions.note: Depends on government pricing decisions; margins recover if retail prices are raised.

rules.mechanism: Refining margins depend on the spread between product and crude prices, not the crude level itself.

conditions.note: Direction is context-dependent: product prices may rise faster or slower than crude.

rules.rationale: Crack spreads are driven by product demand and refinery capacity.

rules.mechanism: Solvents, monomers and other crude derivatives are priced off crude.

conditions.note: Lag of one to two quarters through inventory.

rules.mechanism: Crude-linked raw materials are a meaningful share of paint-makers' costs.

conditions.note: Strong brands can pass costs through with a lag.

rules.mechanism: Russia is a major crude exporter; higher prices raise export revenue for given volumes.

conditions.note: Sanctions-related discounts and price caps reduce realised prices.

rules.rationale: Revenue = price x volume for a large exporter.

rules.mechanism: Higher export earnings raise foreign-currency inflows and support the rouble.

conditions.note: Capital controls and mandatory FX-sale rules distort the relationship.

rules.rationale: Terms-of-trade effect on a commodity-exporter currency.
